69	def build_resource_fields(
70	    payload: object,
71	) -> tuple[str, str, str, str | None]:
72	    """Validate a decoded JSON payload and return normalized field values."""
73	
74	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
75	        raise ResourceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
76	
77	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - _ALLOWED_FIELDS
78	    if unknown_fields:
79	        raise ResourceValidationError(
80	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
81	        )
82	
83	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
84	        if field not in payload:
85	            raise ResourceValidationError(
86	                f"Missing required field: {field!r}."
87	            )
88	
89	    name = _require_non_empty_string(payload["name"], "Name")
90	
91	    category_raw = payload["category"]
92	    if not isinstance(category_raw, str):
93	        raise ResourceValidationError("Category must be a string.")
94	    category = category_raw.lower()
95	    if category not in _CATEGORY_VALUES:
96	        allowed = ", ".join(CATEGORIES)
97	        raise ResourceValidationError(
98	            f"Category must be one of: {allowed} (case-insensitive)."
99	        )
100	
101	    digest_raw = payload["digest"]
102	    if not isinstance(digest_raw, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(
103	        digest_raw
104	    ) is None:
105	        raise ResourceValidationError(
106	            "Digest must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
107	        )
108	    # Hexadecimal digests are case-insensitive; store them canonically.
109	    digest = digest_raw.lower()
110	
111	    source: str | None = None
112	    if "source" in payload:
113	        source = _require_non_empty_string(payload["source"], "Source")
114	
115	    return name, category, digest, source
116

118	def build_dependency_batch_fields(payload: object) -> list[str]:
119	    """Validate a decoded dependency batch payload, returning the id list.
120	
121	    The top level must be a JSON object carrying exactly one field,
122	    ``dependencies``: a non-empty array of at most
123	    :data:`MAX_DEPENDENCY_BATCH_SIZE` non-empty strings, none containing a
124	    path separator (``/`` or ``\\``). The ids are returned in their
125	    submitted order. Duplicates within the array are deliberately not
126	    screened here: their check is ordered after self loops (but before
127	    existing-edge and cycle checks) in :meth:`ResourceStore.add_dependencies`
128	    so that, e.g., a self-referential first entry reports the cycle rather
129	    than the repeat. Existence and graph conflicts are likewise checked
130	    later so their error codes keep precedence.
131	    """
132	
133	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
134	        raise ResourceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
135	
136	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - {"dependencies"}
137	    if unknown_fields:
138	        raise ResourceValidationError(
139	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
140	        )
141	    if "dependencies" not in payload:
142	        raise ResourceValidationError(
143	            "Missing required field: 'dependencies'."
144	        )
145	
146	    items = payload["dependencies"]
147	    if not isinstance(items, list):
148	        raise ResourceValidationError(
149	            "Field 'dependencies' must be an array."
150	        )
151	    if not items:
152	        raise ResourceValidationError(
153	            "Field 'dependencies' must not be empty."
154	        )
155	    if len(items) > MAX_DEPENDENCY_BATCH_SIZE:
156	        raise ResourceValidationError(
157	            f"Field 'dependencies' must not exceed "
158	            f"{MAX_DEPENDENCY_BATCH_SIZE} entries."
159	        )
160	
161	    dependency_ids: list[str] = []
162	    for position, item in enumerate(items):
163	        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item:
164	            raise ResourceValidationError(
165	                f"Dependency at index {position} must be a non-empty string."
166	            )
167	        if "/" in item or "\\" in item:
168	            raise ResourceValidationError(
169	                f"Dependency at index {position} must not contain path "
170	                "separators."
171	            )
172	        dependency_ids.append(item)
173	
174	    return dependency_ids

177	class ResourceStore:
178	    """Process-local, insertion-ordered resource storage."""
179	
180	    def __init__(self) -> None:
181	        self._resources: list[Resource] = []
182	        self._by_id: dict[str, Resource] = {}
183	        self._key_to_id: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str] = {}
184	        # resource id -> ids it directly depends on, and the reverse view.
185	        # Insertion-ordered dicts stand in for ordered sets: membership stays
186	        # O(1) while iteration remembers the order in which each relation was
187	        # established, which the global graph snapshot reports.
188	        self._dependencies: dict[str, dict[str, None]] = {}
189	        self._dependents: dict[str, dict[str, None]] = {}
190	
191	    def reset(self) -> None:
192	        self._resources.clear()
193	        self._resources = []
194	        self._by_id = {}
195	        self._key_to_id = {}
196	        self._dependencies = {}
197	        self._dependents = {}
198	
199	    def list_all(self) -> list[Resource]:
200	        return list(self._resources)
201	
202	    def query(
203	        self,
204	        *,
205	        category: str | None = None,
206	        name: str | None = None,
207	        digest: str | None = None,
208	    ) -> list[Resource]:
209	        """Return matching resources in creation order.
210	
211	        ``category`` is compared case-insensitively, ``name`` is an exact
212	        string match and ``digest`` is compared against the stored lowercase
213	        form. Multiple conditions are AND-ed together.
214	        """
215	
216	        if category is None and name is None and digest is None:
217	            return list(self._resources)
218	
219	        matches: list[Resource] = []
220	        for resource in self._resources:
221	            if category is not None and resource.category != category.lower():
222	                continue
223	            if name is not None and resource.name != name:
224	                continue
225	            if digest is not None and resource.digest != digest:
226	                continue
227	            matches.append(resource)
228	        return matches
229	
230	    def get(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:
231	        return self._by_id.get(resource_id)
232	
233	    def add(
234	        self, payload: object
235	    ) -> tuple[Resource | None, Resource | None]:
236	        """Validate and store a resource.
237	
238	        Returns ``(created, None)`` on success or ``(None, existing)`` when
239	        the same category, name and digest are already registered.
240	        """
241	
242	        name, category, digest, source = build_resource_fields(payload)
243	        key = (category, name, digest)
244	        existing_id = self._key_to_id.get(key)
245	        if existing_id is not None:
246	            return None, self._by_id[existing_id]
247	
248	        resource = Resource(
249	            id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
250	            name=name,
251	            category=category,
252	            digest=digest,
253	            source=source,
254	        )
255	        self._resources.append(resource)
256	        self._by_id[resource.id] = resource
257	        self._key_to_id[key] = resource.id
258	        self._dependencies[resource.id] = {}
259	        self._dependents[resource.id] = {}
260	        return resource, None
261	
262	    def add_remote(
263	        self,
264	        *,
265	        name: str,
266	        category: str,
267	        digest: str,
268	        source: str | None,
269	        resource_id: str | None = None,
270	    ) -> Resource:
271	        """Store a resource resolved from a remote repository.
272	
273	        The caller has already validated the fields and matched the digest
274	        against the registry, so the record is constructed directly; the
275	        same uniqueness key is enforced defensively. When ``resource_id``
276	        is given it is reused (the caller already minted it during
277	        planning); otherwise a fresh id is generated.
278	        """
279	
280	        key = (category, name, digest)
281	        existing_id = self._key_to_id.get(key)
282	        if existing_id is not None:
283	            return self._by_id[existing_id]
284	
285	        resource = Resource(
286	            id=resource_id if resource_id is not None else uuid.uuid4().hex,
287	            name=name,
288	            category=category,
289	            digest=digest,
290	            source=source,
291	        )
292	        self._resources.append(resource)
293	        self._by_id[resource.id] = resource
294	        self._key_to_id[key] = resource.id
295	        self._dependencies[resource.id] = {}
296	        self._dependents[resource.id] = {}
297	        return resource

299	    def discard(self, resource_id: str) -> None:
300	        """Remove a resource that has no edges yet.
301	
302	        Used to roll back a resource created during an aborted operation.
303	        Only safe for resources with no dependencies or dependents.
304	        """
305	
306	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
307	        if resource is None:
308	            return
309	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
310	        self._key_to_id.pop(
311	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
312	        )
313	        self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, None)
314	        self._dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
315	
316	    def remove(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:
317	        """Remove a resource and every dependency edge touching it.
318	
319	        Returns the removed record, or ``None`` when the id is unknown.
320	        Edges the resource started and edges pointing at it disappear
321	        from both graph views; every other resource and edge is left
322	        untouched. The id is never reused by later registrations.
323	        """
324	
325	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
326	        if resource is None:
327	            return None
328	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
329	        self._key_to_id.pop(
330	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
331	        )
332	        for dependency_id in self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, ()):
333	            dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
334	            if dependents is not None:
335	                dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
336	        for dependent_id in self._dependents.pop(resource_id, ()):
337	            dependencies = self._dependencies.get(dependent_id)
338	            if dependencies is not None:
339	                dependencies.pop(resource_id, None)
340	        return resource

342	    # --- Dependencies ------------------------------------------------------
343	
344	    def _reachable(
345	        self, start: str, graph: dict[str, dict[str, None]]
346	    ) -> set[str]:
347	        """Transitive closure of ``start`` through ``graph`` (start excluded)."""
348	
349	        seen: set[str] = set()
350	        stack = list(graph.get(start, ()))
351	        while stack:
352	            node = stack.pop()
353	            if node in seen:
354	                continue
355	            seen.add(node)
356	            stack.extend(graph.get(node, ()))
357	        return seen
358	
359	    def _registration_order(self, ids: set[str]) -> list[str]:
360	        return [r.id for r in self._resources if r.id in ids]
361	
362	    def check_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
363	        """Validate an edge without mutating the graph.
364	
365	        Raises :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency``
366	        when the same-direction relation already exists, or
367	        ``dependency_cycle`` for a self loop or a relation that would
368	        introduce a cycle.
369	        """
370	
371	        if resource_id == dependency_id:
372	            raise DependencyError(
373	                "dependency_cycle", "A resource must not depend on itself."
374	            )
375	
376	        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
377	        if dependency_id in existing:
378	            raise DependencyError(
379	                "duplicate_dependency",
380	                "This dependency relation already exists.",
381	            )
382	
383	        # Adding resource_id -> dependency_id creates a cycle whenever
384	        # dependency_id can already reach resource_id.
385	        if resource_id in self._reachable(dependency_id, self._dependencies):
386	            raise DependencyError(
387	                "dependency_cycle",
388	                "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
389	            )
390	
391	    def add_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
392	        """Record that ``resource_id`` depends on ``dependency_id``.
393	
394	        Both resources must already be registered. Raises
395	        :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency`` when the
396	        same-direction relation already exists, or ``dependency_cycle`` for a
397	        self loop or a relation that would introduce a cycle; in either case
398	        the graph is left unchanged.
399	        """
400	
401	        self.check_dependency(resource_id, dependency_id)
402	        self._dependencies[resource_id][dependency_id] = None
403	        self._dependents[dependency_id][resource_id] = None
404	
405	    def add_dependencies(
406	        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
407	    ) -> None:
408	        """Atomically record several edges out of ``resource_id``.
409	
410	        Both the start and every depended-upon resource must already be
411	        registered (the caller checks existence); ``dependency_ids`` must
412	        come from :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields`, so it is a
413	        non-empty list of non-empty, separator-free strings in submission
414	        order. Conflicts are judged per entry in submission order, and
415	        within one entry in the order self loop, in-batch repeat, existing
416	        same-direction edge, introduced cycle -- the first failure wins.
417	        A self loop or an introduced cycle raises :class:`DependencyError`
418	        with code ``dependency_cycle`` and an existing edge raises one with
419	        code ``duplicate_dependency`` (both 409); an id repeated inside the
420	        batch raises :class:`ResourceValidationError` (400
421	        ``invalid_request``), matching the request-level rule -- but only
422	        once the entry is not itself a self loop, which is checked first.
423	        Every edge in the batch shares the same origin, so an earlier
424	        accepted edge can never feed a path back to the start that did not
425	        already exist; cycle detection therefore uses the committed graph
426	        exactly like :meth:`check_dependency`. The whole batch is atomic: a
427	        failure leaves the graph exactly as it was; on success every edge is
428	        established in submission order.
429	        """
430	
431	        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
432	        accepted: list[str] = []
433	        accepted_set: set[str] = set()
434	        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
435	            if dependency_id == resource_id:
436	                raise DependencyError(
437	                    "dependency_cycle",
438	                    "A resource must not depend on itself.",
439	                )
440	            if dependency_id in accepted_set:
441	                raise ResourceValidationError(
442	                    "A dependency must not be listed more than once in the "
443	                    "same batch."
444	                )
445	            if dependency_id in existing:
446	                raise DependencyError(
447	                    "duplicate_dependency",
448	                    "This dependency relation already exists.",
449	                )
450	            if resource_id in self._reachable(
451	                dependency_id, self._dependencies
452	            ):
453	                raise DependencyError(
454	                    "dependency_cycle",
455	                    "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
456	                )
457	            accepted.append(dependency_id)
458	            accepted_set.add(dependency_id)
459	
460	        # Every check passed; only now mutate, preserving submission order
461	        # in the ordered edge dicts.
462	        for dependency_id in accepted:
463	            self._dependencies[resource_id][dependency_id] = None
464	            self._dependents[dependency_id][resource_id] = None
465	
466	    def has_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> bool:
467	        """Return whether the direct edge ``resource_id -> dependency_id`` exists."""
468	
469	        return dependency_id in self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
470	
471	    def remove_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> bool:
472	        """Remove only the direct edge from ``resource_id`` to ``dependency_id``.
473	
474	        Returns ``True`` when the edge existed and was removed, ``False``
475	        when there was no such direct edge. Neither resource record nor any
476	        other edge is touched; transitive relations that survive through
477	        other paths are left to be recomputed by the read views.
478	        """
479	
480	        dependencies = self._dependencies.get(resource_id)
481	        if dependencies is None or dependency_id not in dependencies:
482	            return False
483	        del dependencies[dependency_id]
484	        dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
485	        if dependents is not None:
486	            dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
487	        return True
488	
489	    def list_dependencies(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
490	        """Return every reachable dependency id in registration order."""
491	
492	        return self._registration_order(
493	            self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependencies)
494	        )

496	    def shortest_path(self, start: str, end: str) -> list[str] | None:
497	        """Return the shortest directed path from ``start`` to ``end``.
498	
499	        The path follows dependency edges in their direction (the start
500	        resource depends on the end resource) and is reported as the list
501	        of node ids, ``start`` first and ``end`` last, with no repeated
502	        nodes. ``start == end`` yields the single-node path. Returns
503	        ``None`` when ``end`` is not reachable from ``start``. Among
504	        equally short paths the one whose nodes come earliest in
505	        registration order -- compared from the second node onward -- is
506	        picked, so the answer is stable.
507	        """
508	
509	        if start == end:
510	            return [start]
511	
512	        # Hops from every node to ``end`` along the edge direction,
513	        # computed as a breadth-first walk over the reverse graph.
514	        dist: dict[str, int] = {end: 0}
515	        queue = [end]
516	        for node in queue:
517	            for predecessor in self._dependents.get(node, ()):
518	                if predecessor not in dist:
519	                    dist[predecessor] = dist[node] + 1
520	                    queue.append(predecessor)
521	        if start not in dist:
522	            return None
523	
524	        order = {
525	            resource.id: index
526	            for index, resource in enumerate(self._resources)
527	        }
528	        path = [start]
529	        current = start
530	        while current != end:
531	            remaining = dist[current]
532	            # Every candidate continues on a shortest path; taking the
533	            # earliest-registered one at each step yields the stable pick.
534	            current = min(
535	                (
536	                    successor
537	                    for successor in self._dependencies.get(current, ())
538	                    if dist.get(successor) == remaining - 1
539	                ),
540	                key=lambda node: order[node],
541	            )
542	            path.append(current)
543	        return path
544	
545	    def all_shortest_paths(
546	        self, start: str, end: str
547	    ) -> list[list[str]] | None:
548	        """Return every shortest directed path from ``start`` to ``end``.
549	
550	        Each path follows dependency edges in their direction (the start
551	        resource depends on the end resource) and is reported as the list
552	        of node ids, ``start`` first and ``end`` last, with no repeated
553	        nodes. ``start == end`` yields the single single-node path.
554	        Returns ``None`` when ``end`` is not reachable from ``start``.
555	        The paths are ordered stably: by the second node's registration
556	        order first, then by each subsequent node's registration order.
557	        """
558	
559	        if start == end:
560	            return [[start]]
561	
562	        # Hops from every node to ``end`` along the edge direction,
563	        # computed as a breadth-first walk over the reverse graph.
564	        dist: dict[str, int] = {end: 0}
565	        queue = [end]
566	        for node in queue:
567	            for predecessor in self._dependents.get(node, ()):
568	                if predecessor not in dist:
569	                    dist[predecessor] = dist[node] + 1
570	                    queue.append(predecessor)
571	        if start not in dist:
572	            return None
573	
574	        # Enumerate every shortest path: from each node only the successors
575	        # exactly one hop closer to ``end`` can continue a shortest path.
576	        # The graph is a DAG, so the walk always terminates.
577	        paths: list[list[str]] = []
578	        stack: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = [(start, [start])]
579	        while stack:
580	            node, path = stack.pop()
581	            if node == end:
582	                paths.append(path)
583	                continue
584	            remaining = dist[node]
585	            for successor in self._dependencies.get(node, ()):
586	                if dist.get(successor) == remaining - 1:
587	                    stack.append((successor, [*path, successor]))
588	
589	        order = {
590	            resource.id: index
591	            for index, resource in enumerate(self._resources)
592	        }
593	        paths.sort(
594	            key=lambda path: tuple(order[node] for node in path[1:])
595	        )
596	        return paths
597	
598	    def list_impact(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
599	        """Return ids that directly or transitively depend on ``resource_id``.
600	
601	        The start resource itself is excluded; results are in registration
602	        order.
603	        """

605	        return self._registration_order(
606	            self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependents)
607	        )

611	    def list_direct_dependencies(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
612	        """Return the ids ``resource_id`` directly depends on.
613	
614	        Only direct outbound edges, in the order the relations were
615	        established; the transitive closure is left to
616	        :meth:`list_dependencies`.
617	        """
618	
619	        return list(self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ()))
620	
621	    def list_direct_dependents(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
622	        """Return the ids that directly depend on ``resource_id``.
623	
624	        Only direct inbound edges, in the order the relations were
625	        established; the transitive closure is left to :meth:`list_impact`.
626	        """
627	
628	        return list(self._dependents.get(resource_id, ()))
629	
630	    def list_edges(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
631	        """Return every direct edge as ``(resource_id, dependency_id)``.
632	
633	        Edges are grouped by the start resource's registration order; within
634	        one start resource they follow the order in which each relation was
635	        established. Manually registered and cross-reference-resolved edges
636	        are reported alike, since both flow through
637	        :meth:`add_dependency`.
638	        """
639	
640	        return [
641	            (resource.id, dependency_id)
642	            for resource in self._resources
643	            for dependency_id in self._dependencies.get(resource.id, ())
644	        ]
645	
646	    def graph_stats(self) -> dict[str, object]:
647	        """Compute whole-graph statistics from the current registry.
648	
649	        Counts nodes and direct edges, lists isolated resources, ranks
650	        resources by out/in degree and measures the longest dependency
651	        chain (in nodes). Manually registered and cross-reference-resolved
652	        edges are counted alike, since both flow through
653	        :meth:`add_dependency`. Everything is derived on the fly.
654	        """
655	
656	        ids = [resource.id for resource in self._resources]
657	        out_degree = {
658	            resource_id: len(self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ()))
659	            for resource_id in ids
660	        }
661	        in_degree = {
662	            resource_id: len(self._dependents.get(resource_id, ()))
663	            for resource_id in ids
664	        }
665	
666	        isolated = [
667	            resource_id
668	            for resource_id in ids
669	            if out_degree[resource_id] == 0 and in_degree[resource_id] == 0
670	        ]
671	
672	        # The graph is a DAG (cycles are rejected at registration time), so
673	        # the longest chain is the maximum successor-path depth. The
674	        # iterative postorder walk avoids any recursion limit on long
675	        # chains; ``depth`` counts nodes, so an isolated node scores one.
676	        depth: dict[str, int] = {}
677	        for root in ids:
678	            stack: list[tuple[str, bool]] = [(root, False)]
679	            while stack:
680	                node, expanded = stack.pop()
681	                if node in depth:
682	                    continue
683	                successors = self._dependencies.get(node, ())
684	                if not expanded:
685	                    stack.append((node, True))
686	                    for successor in successors:
687	                        if successor not in depth:
688	                            stack.append((successor, False))
689	                    continue
690	                depth[node] = (
691	                    1
692	                    if not successors
693	                    else 1 + max(depth[successor] for successor in successors)
694	                )
695	        max_depth = max((depth[resource_id] for resource_id in ids), default=0)
696	
697	        def ranking(counts: dict[str, int]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
698	            # ``sorted`` is stable, so equal degrees keep registration order.
699	            ordered = sorted(
700	                (
701	                    (resource_id, counts[resource_id])
702	                    for resource_id in ids
703	                    if counts[resource_id] > 0
704	                ),
705	                key=lambda item: -item[1],
706	            )
707	            return [

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import unittest

from provenance_api.app import application, reset_state, store

DIGESTS = {ch: ch * 64 for ch in "abcdefgh"}


def call(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], bytes]:
    if body is None:
        payload = b""
    elif isinstance(body, dict):
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    else:
        payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body

    environ: dict[str, object] = {
        "REQUEST_METHOD": method,
        "PATH_INFO": path,
        "QUERY_STRING": query_string if query_string is not None else "",
        "CONTENT_LENGTH": str(len(payload)),
        "CONTENT_TYPE": "application/json",
        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(payload),
    }
    captured: dict[str, object] = {}

    def start_response(status: str, headers: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        captured["status"] = status
        captured["headers"] = headers

    chunks = application(environ, start_response)
    return str(captured["status"]), list(captured["headers"]), b"".join(chunks)


def call_json(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
    status, headers, raw = call(method, path, body, query_string=query_string)
    return status, headers, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))


class DependencyBatchTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        reset_state()

    def _create(self, ch: str) -> str:
        _s, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources",
            {"name": f"r-{ch}", "category": "code", "digest": DIGESTS[ch]},
        )
        return str(body["id"])

    def _batch(
        self,
        start: str,
        items: object,
        *,
        query_string: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
        return call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{start}/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": items},
            query_string=query_string,
        )

    # --- Success -----------------------------------------------------------

    def test_batch_creates_every_edge_and_echoes_in_submission_order(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        c = self._create("c")

        status, headers, body = self._batch(a, [c, b])
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(
            headers[0], ("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            body,
            {
                "dependencies": [
                    {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": c},
                    {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": b},
                ]
            },
        )
        # Every entry keeps the single-registration fixed key order.
        self.assertEqual(
            [list(entry) for entry in body["dependencies"]],
            [["resource_id", "dependency_id"], ["resource_id", "dependency_id"]],
        )

        # The edges land in the graph views immediately.
        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(set(deps["dependencies"]), {b, c})
        for target in (b, c):
            _s, _h, impact = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{target}/impact")
            self.assertEqual(impact["resources"], [a])

    def test_response_is_compact_json_with_single_newline(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        _s, _h, raw = call(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": [b]},
        )
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertFalse(raw.endswith(b"\n\n"))
        self.assertNotIn(b" ", raw[:-1])
        self.assertEqual(
            raw,
            b'{"dependencies":[{"resource_id":"' + a.encode()
            + b'","dependency_id":"' + b.encode() + b'"}]}\n',
        )

    def test_edges_keep_submission_order_in_direct_listing(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b, c, d = self._create("b"), self._create("c"), self._create("d")

        status, _h, _b = self._batch(a, [d, b, c])
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [d, b, c])

    def test_indirectly_reachable_missing_direct_edge_is_still_created(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        c = self._create("c")
        self.assertEqual(
            call_json(
                "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies", {"dependency_id": b}
            )[0],
            "201 Created",
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            call_json(
                "POST", f"/resources/{b}/dependencies", {"dependency_id": c}
            )[0],
            "201 Created",
        )
        # c is already reachable from a transitively, but no direct edge.
        self.assertFalse(store.has_dependency(a, c))
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [c])
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(
            body,
            {"dependencies": [{"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": c}]},
        )
        self.assertTrue(store.has_dependency(a, c))

    def test_batch_of_one_hundred_existing_resources_succeeds(self) -> None:
        start = self._create("a")
        others = [
            str(
                call_json(
                    "POST",
                    "/resources",
                    {
                        "name": f"r-{index}",
                        "category": "code",
                        "digest": f"{index:064x}",
                    },
                )[2]["id"]
            )
            for index in range(100)
        ]
        status, _h, body = self._batch(start, others)
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry["dependency_id"] for entry in body["dependencies"]], others
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(store.list_direct_dependencies(start)), 100)

    def test_successive_batches_accumulate_without_duplicates(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        c = self._create("c")
        self.assertEqual(self._batch(a, [b])[0], "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(self._batch(a, [c])[0], "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [b, c])

    # --- Body / parameter validation (400) --------------------------------

    def test_missing_body_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch", None
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_malformed_or_non_utf8_body_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch", b"{bad"
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

        status, _h, raw = call(
            "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch", b"\xff\xfe"
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(raw)["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_non_object_top_level_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        for bad in (b"[]", b'"x"', b"42", b"null"):
            with self.subTest(bad=bad):
                status, _h, body = call_json(
                    "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch", bad
                )
                self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
                self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_missing_or_unknown_field_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        for payload in ({}, {"extra": 1}, {"dependencies": [b], "extra": 1}):
            with self.subTest(payload=payload):
                status, _h, body = call_json(
                    "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch", payload
                )
                self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
                self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_dependencies_not_an_array_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        for bad in ("x", 5, True, None, {"id": "x"}):
            with self.subTest(bad=bad):
                status, _h, body = call_json(
                    "POST",
                    f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch",
                    {"dependencies": bad},
                )
                self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
                self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_empty_array_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [])
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_more_than_one_hundred_entries_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [f"x{i:03d}" for i in range(101)])
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_invalid_entry_values_are_bad_request(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        for bad in (5, True, None, ["x"], {"id": "x"}, "", "x/y", "x\\y"):
            with self.subTest(bad=bad):
                status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [bad])
                self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
                self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    def test_whitespace_entry_is_syntactically_an_id_so_missing_not_400(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, ["   "])
        self.assertEqual(status, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "resource_not_found")

    def test_in_batch_duplicate_is_bad_request_and_creates_nothing(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        c = self._create("c")
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [c, b, c])
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [])

    def test_query_parameters_are_rejected_before_business_data(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [b], query_string="x=1")
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [])

    def test_separator_in_start_id_is_bad_request(self) -> None:
        b = self._create("b")
        for raw in ("a/b", "a\\b"):
            status, _h, body = call_json(
                "POST",
                f"/resources/{raw}/dependencies/batch",
                {"dependencies": [b]},
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
            self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    # --- Existence (404) ---------------------------------------------------

    def test_missing_start_returns_not_found_even_when_dep_missing(self) -> None:
        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources/missing/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": ["also-missing"]},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "resource_not_found")

    def test_missing_dependency_returns_not_found_and_builds_nothing(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        phantom = "0" * 32
        # The valid earlier entry must not be left half-created.
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [b, phantom])
        self.assertEqual(status, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "resource_not_found")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [])

    def test_body_validation_outranks_missing_resources(self) -> None:
        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources/missing/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": ["bad/id"]},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")

    # --- Conflicts (409) ---------------------------------------------------

    def test_self_loop_is_dependency_cycle(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [b, a])
        self.assertEqual(status, "409 Conflict")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_cycle")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [])

    def test_self_loop_outranks_in_batch_duplicate(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        # The repeated entry is itself the start id; self loop reports first.
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [a, a])
        self.assertEqual(status, "409 Conflict")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_cycle")

    def test_existing_same_direction_edge_is_duplicate_dependency(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        c = self._create("c")
        self.assertEqual(self._batch(a, [b])[0], "201 Created")
        # c earlier in the same request must not survive the conflict on b.
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [c, b])
        self.assertEqual(status, "409 Conflict")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "duplicate_dependency")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [b])

    def test_duplicate_outranks_cycle_for_the_same_entry(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        # b -> a makes adding a -> b both an existing edge (none yet) ... set
        # up an existing edge a -> b first, plus the reverse path.
        self.assertEqual(
            call_json(
                "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies", {"dependency_id": b}
            )[0],
            "201 Created",
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            call_json(
                "POST", f"/resources/{b}/dependencies", {"dependency_id": a}
            )[0],
            "409 Conflict",
        )
        # a -> b already exists, so re-adding via batch is duplicate, even
        # though the reverse edge could never coexist either.
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [b])
        self.assertEqual(status, "409 Conflict")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "duplicate_dependency")

    def test_edge_that_would_introduce_cycle_is_rejected_atomically(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        c = self._create("c")
        d = self._create("d")
        self.assertEqual(
            call_json(
                "POST", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies", {"dependency_id": b}
            )[0],
            "201 Created",

        self.assertEqual(
            call_json(
                "POST", f"/resources/{b}/dependencies", {"dependency_id": c}
            )[0],
            "201 Created",
        )
        # Closing c -> a cycles; an earlier valid d edge must not persist.
        status, _h, body = self._batch(c, [d, a])
        self.assertEqual(status, "409 Conflict")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_cycle")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(c), [])
        _s, _h, impact_d = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{d}/impact")
        self.assertEqual(impact_d["resources"], [])

    def test_transitive_cycle_across_batch_candidate_is_detected(self) -> None:

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import unittest

from provenance_api.app import application, reset_state
from provenance_api.cross_references import Resolution

DIGEST_A = "a" * 64
DIGEST_B = "b" * 64
DIGEST_C = "c" * 64
DIGEST_D = "d" * 64

UPSTREAM = "https://repo.example.invalid"
REMOTE_ID = "remote-42"
REMOTE_NAME = "remote-model"
DIGEST_REMOTE = "f" * 64
SOURCE = "https://repo.example.invalid/sources/remote-42"


def call(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
    omit_content_length: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], bytes]:
    if body is None:
        payload = b""
    elif isinstance(body, dict):
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    else:
        payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body

    environ: dict[str, object] = {
        "REQUEST_METHOD": method,
        "PATH_INFO": path,
        "QUERY_STRING": query_string if query_string is not None else "",
        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(payload),
    }
    if not omit_content_length:
        environ["CONTENT_LENGTH"] = str(len(payload))
    captured: dict[str, object] = {}

    def start_response(status: str, headers: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        captured["status"] = status
        captured["headers"] = headers

    chunks = application(environ, start_response)
    return str(captured["status"]), list(captured["headers"]), b"".join(chunks)


def call_json(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    **kwargs: object,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
    status, headers, raw = call(method, path, body, **kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return status, headers, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))


class DependencyDeleteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        reset_state()

    def _create(self, name: str, digest: str) -> str:
        _s, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources",
            {"name": name, "category": "code", "digest": digest},
        )
        return str(body["id"])

    def _add(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
        status, _h, _b = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies",
            {"dependency_id": dependency_id},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")

    def _delete(
        self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str
    ) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
        return call_json(
            "DELETE",
            f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies/{dependency_id}",
        )

    # --- Success and response shape ----------------------------------------

    def test_delete_returns_200_echoing_relation_in_registration_key_order(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)

        status, headers, body = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")
        self.assertEqual(
            list(body), ["resource_id", "dependency_id"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(body, {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": b})
        self.assertEqual(
            headers[0], ("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        )

    def test_delete_body_is_compact_json_ending_with_single_newline(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)

        _s, _h, raw = call(
            "DELETE", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/{b}"
        )
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertFalse(raw.endswith(b"\n\n"))
        self.assertNotIn(b" ", raw[:-1])
        self.assertEqual(
            raw,
            b'{"resource_id":"' + a.encode() + b'","dependency_id":"'
            + b.encode() + b'"}\n',
        )

    # --- Graph semantics ----------------------------------------------------

    def test_only_the_direct_edge_is_removed(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(b, c)
        self._add(a, c)

        status, _h, _b = self._delete(a, c)
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        # a still reaches c through a -> b -> c.
        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [b, c])
        # The direct edge itself is gone from b's inbound view.
        _s, _h, impact_c = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{c}/impact")
        self.assertEqual(impact_c["resources"], [a, b])

    def test_removing_edge_on_one_path_leaves_other_direct_edges_intact(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(a, c)
        self._add(b, c)

        self._delete(a, c)

        _s, _h, deps_a = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps_a["dependencies"], [b, c])
        _s, _h, deps_b = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{b}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps_b["dependencies"], [c])

    def test_re_registering_same_direction_recreates_edge_as_201(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._delete(a, b)

        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{a}/dependencies",
            {"dependency_id": b},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(body, {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": b})

        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [b])

    def test_resource_records_are_not_touched(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._delete(a, b)

        _s, _h, listing = call_json("GET", "/resources")
        self.assertEqual(
            sorted(r["id"] for r in listing["resources"]), sorted([a, b])
        )
        for resource_id in (a, b):
            status, _h, _r = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{resource_id}")
            self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

    def test_deleted_edge_drops_from_release_blockers(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)
        status, _h, _b = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{b}/lifecycle",
            {"state": "quarantined", "reason": "suspect"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        _s, _h, blockers = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{a}/release-blockers"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            blockers["blockers"],
            [{"resource_id": b, "state": "quarantined"}],
        )

        self._delete(a, b)

        _s, _h, blockers = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{a}/release-blockers"
        )
        self.assertEqual(blockers["blockers"], [])
        self.assertNotIn("dependency_blocked", blockers["reasons"])

    def test_deleted_edge_drops_from_vulnerability_impact_closure(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(b, c)
        status, _h, _b = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{c}/vulnerabilities",
            {
                "advisory": "CVE-1",
                "component": "lib",
                "severity": "high",
                "summary": "a bug",
            },
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")

        self._delete(b, c)

        _s, _h, impacts = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependency-vulnerability-impact"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry["resource_id"] for entry in impacts["impacts"]], [a, b]
        )
        # b itself still surfaces the edge's absence by reaching nothing.
        _s, _h, b_impacts = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{b}/dependency-vulnerability-impact"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry["resource_id"] for entry in b_impacts["impacts"]], [b]
        )

    # --- Not found ----------------------------------------------------------

    def test_missing_edge_returns_dependency_not_found(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)

        status, _h, body = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(status, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_not_found")

    def test_repeat_delete_returns_dependency_not_found(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(a, c)

        first, _h, _b = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(first, "200 OK")
        second, _h, body = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(second, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_not_found")

        # Other relations and resources are unaffected by the repeated delete.
        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [c])

    def test_missing_start_resource_returns_resource_not_found(self) -> None:
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        phantom = "0" * 32

        status, _h, body = self._delete(phantom, b)
        self.assertEqual(status, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "resource_not_found")

        _s, _h, listing = call_json("GET", "/resources")
        self.assertEqual(len(listing["resources"]), 1)

    def test_edge_to_deregistered_dependency_returns_dependency_not_found(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)

class CrossReferenceEdgeDeleteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        reset_state()

    def _local(self) -> str:
        _s, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources",

        )
        return str(body["id"])

    def test_cross_reference_edge_is_removed_but_record_remains(self) -> None:
        from unittest import mock

        resource_id = self._local()
        resolution = Resolution(
            name=REMOTE_NAME,
            category="model",
            digest=DIGEST_REMOTE,
            source=SOURCE,
            raw=b"{}",
        )
        reference_body = {
            "repository": "partner",
            "upstream": UPSTREAM,
            "remote_id": REMOTE_ID,
            "digest": DIGEST_REMOTE,
        }
        with mock.patch(
            "provenance_api.app.resolve_remote", return_value=resolution
        ):
            status, _h, _b = call_json(
                "POST",
                f"/resources/{resource_id}/cross-references",
                reference_body,
            )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")

        _s, _h, listing = call_json("GET", "/resources")
        self.assertEqual(len(listing["resources"]), 2)
        remote_id = next(
            r["id"] for r in listing["resources"] if r["id"] != resource_id
        )

        # The edge participates in the topology before deletion.
        _s, _h, deps = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies"
        )
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [remote_id])

        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "DELETE",
            f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies/{remote_id}",
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")
        self.assertEqual(
            body, {"resource_id": resource_id, "dependency_id": remote_id}
        )

        # The reference record and the resolved local resource are untouched.
        _s, _h, refs = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{resource_id}/cross-references"
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(refs["cross_references"]), 1)
        _s, _h, listing = call_json("GET", "/resources")
        self.assertEqual(len(listing["resources"]), 2)

        # The edge is gone from every graph view.
        _s, _h, deps = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies"
        )
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [])
        _s, _h, impact = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{remote_id}/impact"
        )
        self.assertEqual(impact["resources"], [])

        # Re-submitting the same reference is still rejected as a duplicate
        # reference and does not rebuild the edge.
        with mock.patch(
            "provenance_api.app.resolve_remote", return_value=resolution
        ):
            status, _h, body = call_json(
                "POST",
                f"/resources/{resource_id}/cross-references",
                reference_body,
            )
        self.assertEqual(status, "409 Conflict")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "duplicate_reference")
        _s, _h, deps = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies"
        )

- 路径标识为空，或含 `/`、`\\`，返回 HTTP 400（错误码 `invalid_request`），不执行任何操作。

def add_dependencies(
        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
    ) -> None:
        """Atomically record several edges out of ``resource_id``.

        Both the start and every depended-upon resource must already be
        registered (the caller checks existence); ``dependency_ids`` must
        come from :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields`, so it is a
        non-empty list of non-empty, separator-free strings in submission
        order. Conflicts are judged per entry in submission order, and
        within one entry in the order self loop, in-batch repeat, existing
        same-direction edge, introduced cycle -- the first failure wins.
        A self loop or an introduced cycle raises :class:`DependencyError`
        with code ``dependency_cycle`` and an existing edge raises one with
        code ``duplicate_dependency`` (both 409); an id repeated inside the
        batch raises :class:`ResourceValidationError` (400
        ``invalid_request``), matching the request-level rule -- but only
        once the entry is not itself a self loop, which is checked first.
        Every edge in the batch shares the same origin, so an earlier
        accepted edge can never feed a path back to the start that did not
        already exist; cycle detection therefore uses the committed graph
        exactly like :meth:`check_dependency`. The whole batch is atomic: a
        failure leaves the graph exactly as it was; on success every edge
        is established in submission order.
        """

        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
        accepted: list[str] = []
        accepted_set: set[str] = set()
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            if dependency_id == resource_id:
                raise DependencyError(
                    "dependency_cycle",
                    "A resource must not depend on itself.",
                )
            if dependency_id in accepted_set:
                raise ResourceValidationError(
                    "A dependency must not be listed more than once in the "
                    "same batch."
                )
            if dependency_id in existing:
                raise DependencyError(
                    "duplicate_dependency",
                    "This dependency relation already exists.",
                )
            if resource_id in self._reachable(
                dependency_id, self._dependencies
            ):
                raise DependencyError(
                    "dependency_cycle",
                    "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
                )
            accepted.append(dependency_id)
            accepted_set.add(dependency_id)

        # Every check passed; only now mutate, preserving submission order
        # in the ordered edge dicts.
        for dependency_id in accepted:

def add_dependencies(
        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
    ) -> None:
        """Atomically record several edges out of ``resource_id``.

        Both the start and every depended-upon resource must already be
        registered (the caller checks existence); ``dependency_ids`` must
        come from :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields`, so it is a
        non-empty list of non-empty, separator-free strings in submission
        order. Conflict precedence is a fixed rule order, not the
        submission position: the whole batch is first screened for self
        loops, then for repeats inside the batch, then for existing
        same-direction edges, and finally for edges that would introduce a
        cycle. When several entries hit different rules at once, only the
        foremost rule is reported; within one rule the earliest submission
        position wins. A self loop or an introduced cycle raises
        :class:`DependencyError` with code ``dependency_cycle`` and an
        existing edge raises one with code ``duplicate_dependency`` (both
        409); an id repeated inside the batch raises
        :class:`ResourceValidationError` (400 ``invalid_request``), but
        only when no entry is a self loop, which is screened first. Every
        edge in the batch shares the same origin, so an earlier accepted
        edge can never feed a path back to the start that did not already
        exist; cycle detection therefore uses the committed graph exactly
        like :meth:`check_dependency`. The whole batch is atomic: a
        failure leaves the graph exactly as it was; on success every edge
        is established in submission order.
        """

        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())

        # Each pass is read-only; the graph is touched only once every rule
        # has passed, which makes the precedence independent of where in
        # the batch each conflict sits and guarantees all-or-nothing
        # behavior.
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            if dependency_id == resource_id:
                raise DependencyError(
                    "dependency_cycle",
                    "A resource must not depend on itself.",
                )

        seen: set[str] = set()
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            if dependency_id in seen:
                raise ResourceValidationError(
                    "A dependency must not be listed more than once in the "
                    "same batch."
                )
            seen.add(dependency_id)

        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            if dependency_id in existing:
                raise DependencyError(
                    "duplicate_dependency",
                    "This dependency relation already exists.",
                )

        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            if resource_id in self._reachable(
                dependency_id, self._dependencies
            ):
                raise DependencyError(
                    "dependency_cycle",
                    "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
                )

        # Every check passed; only now mutate, preserving submission order
        # in the ordered edge dicts.
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            self._dependencies[resource_id][dependency_id] = None
            self._dependents[dependency_id][resource_id] = None

    def remove_dependencies(
        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
    ) -> None:
        """Atomically remove several direct edges out of ``resource_id``.

        The start resource must already be registered (the caller checks
        existence); ``dependency_ids`` comes from
        :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields` with duplicate rejection on,
        so it is a non-empty list of distinct, non-empty, separator-free
        strings in submission order. Every listed direct edge must
        currently exist; the first submission position without such an
        edge raises :class:`DependencyError` with code
        ``dependency_not_found`` and no edge is removed, so a repeat of a
        failed request reports the same missing relation. Only when every
        edge is present are they all removed; resource records and every
        other edge are left untouched, and transitive relations that
        survive through other paths are recomputed by the read views.
        """

        dependencies = self._dependencies.get(resource_id)
        if dependencies is None:
            raise DependencyError(
                "dependency_not_found",
                "No direct dependency relation exists from this resource "
                "to the requested dependency.",
            )
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            if dependency_id not in dependencies:
                raise DependencyError(
                    "dependency_not_found",
                    "No direct dependency relation exists from this "
                    "resource to the requested dependency.",
                )

        # Every edge exists; remove them all, after the read-only checks,
        # so a missing entry can never leave the batch half-deleted.
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            del dependencies[dependency_id]
            dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
            if dependents is not None:
                dependents.pop(resource_id, None)

def remove_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> bool:
        """Remove only the direct edge from ``resource_id`` to ``dependency_id``.

        Returns ``True`` when the edge existed and was removed, ``False``
        when there was no such direct edge. Neither resource record nor any
        other edge is touched; transitive relations that survive through
        other paths are left to be recomputed by the read views.
        """

        dependencies = self._dependencies.get(resource_id)
        if dependencies is None or dependency_id not in dependencies:
            return False
        del dependencies[dependency_id]
        dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
        if dependents is not None:
            dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
        return True

        """Return every reachable dependency id in registration order."""

    def remove_dependencies(
        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
    ) -> None:
        """Atomically remove several direct edges out of ``resource_id``.

        The start resource must already be registered (the caller checks
        existence); ``dependency_ids`` comes from
        :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields` with duplicate rejection on,
        so it is a non-empty list of distinct, non-empty, separator-free
        strings in submission order. Every listed direct edge must
        currently exist; the first submission position without such an
        edge raises :class:`DependencyError` with code
        ``dependency_not_found`` and no edge is removed, so a repeat of a
        failed request reports the same missing relation. Only when every
        edge is present are they all removed; resource records and every
        other edge are left untouched, and transitive relations that
        survive through other paths are recomputed by the read views.
        """

        dependencies = self._dependencies.get(resource_id)
        if dependencies is None:
            raise DependencyError(
                "dependency_not_found",
                "No direct dependency relation exists from this resource "
                "to the requested dependency.",
            )
        # Read-only pass first: a missing entry must never leave the batch
        # half-deleted. The first absent position wins, in submission order.
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            if dependency_id not in dependencies:
                raise DependencyError(
                    "dependency_not_found",
                    "No direct dependency relation exists from this "
                    "resource to the requested dependency.",
                )

        # Every edge exists; remove them all after the checks.
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:
            del dependencies[dependency_id]
            dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
            if dependents is not None:
                dependents.pop(resource_id, None)

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import unittest

from provenance_api.app import application, reset_state, store

DIGESTS = {ch: ch * 64 for ch in "abcdefgh"}


def call(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], bytes]:
    if body is None:
        payload = b""
    elif isinstance(body, dict):
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    else:
        payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body

    environ: dict[str, object] = {
        "REQUEST_METHOD": method,
        "PATH_INFO": path,
        "QUERY_STRING": query_string if query_string is not None else "",
        "CONTENT_LENGTH": str(len(payload)),
        "CONTENT_TYPE": "application/json",
        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(payload),
    }
    captured: dict[str, object] = {}

    def start_response(status: str, headers: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        captured["status"] = status
        captured["headers"] = headers

    chunks = application(environ, start_response)
    return str(captured["status"]), list(captured["headers"]), b"".join(chunks)


def call_json(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
    status, headers, raw = call(method, path, body, query_string=query_string)
    return status, headers, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))


class DependencyBatchDeleteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        reset_state()

    def _create(self, ch: str) -> str:
        _s, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources",
            {"name": f"r-{ch}", "category": "code", "digest": DIGESTS[ch]},
        )
        return str(body["id"])

    def _add_edges(self, start: str, items: list[str]) -> None:
        status, _h, _b = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{start}/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": items},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")

    def _delete_batch(
        self,
        start: str,
        items: object,
        *,
        query_string: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
        return call_json(
            "DELETE",
            f"/resources/{start}/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": items},
            query_string=query_string,
        )

    # --- Success -----------------------------------------------------------

    def test_batch_removes_every_edge_and_echoes_in_submission_order(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        c = self._create("c")
        d = self._create("d")
        self._add_edges(a, [b, c, d])

        status, headers, body = self._delete_batch(a, [d, b])
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")
        self.assertEqual(
            headers[0], ("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            body,
            {
                "dependencies": [
                    {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": d},
                    {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": b},
                ]
            },
        )
        # Every entry keeps the single-registration fixed key order.
        self.assertEqual(
            [list(entry) for entry in body["dependencies"]],
            [["resource_id", "dependency_id"], ["resource_id", "dependency_id"]],
        )

        # Only the remaining edge survives in the graph views.
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [c])
        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [c])
        for removed, kept in ((b, c), (d, c)):
            _s, _h, impact = call_json(
                "GET", f"/resources/{removed}/impact"
            )
            self.assertEqual(impact["resources"], [])
        _s, _h, impact_c = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{c}/impact")
        self.assertEqual(impact_c["resources"], [a])

    def test_response_is_compact_json_with_single_newline(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        self._add_edges(a, [b])
        _s, _h, raw = call(
            "DELETE",
            f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": [b]},
        )
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertFalse(raw.endswith(b"\n\n"))
        self.assertNotIn(b" ", raw[:-1])
        self.assertEqual(
            raw,
            b'{"dependencies":[{"resource_id":"' + a.encode()
            + b'","dependency_id":"' + b.encode() + b'"}]}\n',
        )

    def test_remaining_edges_keep_their_established_order(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b, c, d = self._create("b"), self._create("c"), self._create("d")
        self._add_edges(a, [d, b, c])

        status, _h, _b = self._delete_batch(a, [b])
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [d, c])

    def test_batch_of_one_hundred_edges_succeeds(self) -> None:
        start = self._create("a")
        others = [
            str(
                call_json(
                    "POST",
                    "/resources",
                    {
                        "name": f"r-{index}",
                        "category": "code",
                        "digest": f"{index:064x}",
                    },
                )[2]["id"]
            )
            for index in range(100)
        ]
        self._add_edges(start, others)

        status, _h, body = self._delete_batch(start, others)
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry["dependency_id"] for entry in body["dependencies"]], others
        )
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(start), [])

    def test_transitive_relation_via_surviving_path_stays_visible(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")

DIGESTS = {ch: ch * 64 for ch in "abcdefgh"}


def call(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], bytes]:
    if body is None:
        payload = b""
    elif isinstance(body, dict):
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    else:
        payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body

    environ: dict[str, object] = {
        "REQUEST_METHOD": method,
        "PATH_INFO": path,
        "QUERY_STRING": query_string if query_string is not None else "",
        "CONTENT_LENGTH": str(len(payload)),
        "CONTENT_TYPE": "application/json",
        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(payload),
    }
    captured: dict[str, object] = {}

    def start_response(status: str, headers: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        captured["status"] = status
        captured["headers"] = headers

    chunks = application(environ, start_response)
    return str(captured["status"]), list(captured["headers"]), b"".join(chunks)

    method: str,

    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:

class DependencyBatchRegistrationPrecedenceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The fixed registration rule order ignores submission position."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        reset_state()

    def _create(self, ch: str) -> str:
        _s, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources",

        )
        return str(body["id"])

    def _batch(
        self, start: str, items: object
    ) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
        return call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{start}/dependencies/batch",
            {"dependencies": items},
        )

    def test_self_loop_rule_beats_earlier_duplicate_edge(self) -> None:
        # The existing-edge conflict sits at position 0 and the self loop
        # at position 1; the fixed rule order reports the self loop.
        a = self._create("a")
        b = self._create("b")
        self.assertEqual(self._batch(a, [b])[0], "201 Created")
        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [b, a])
        self.assertEqual(status, "409 Conflict")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_cycle")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [b])

        a = self._create("a")

        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_cycle")

        status, _h, body = self._batch(a, [b, b, c])
        self.assertEqual(status, "400 Bad Request")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "invalid_request")
        self.assertEqual(store.list_direct_dependencies(a), [c])

content.text:
Everything is complete and verified. Here's a summary of the change.

## Summary

Added symmetric **batch dependency removal** and codified the batch-registration conflict order as a position-independent rule.

### `provenance_api/resources.py`
- `build_dependency_batch_fields()` gained a `reject_duplicates` flag. Registration keeps repeats out of the builder (self-loop precedence lives in the store); removal passes `reject_duplicates=True` so in-array duplicates fail at request-validation time, before any business data is read.
- `add_dependencies()` rewritten from a per-position loop to **four read-only passes in fixed rule order** — self-loop → in-batch repeat → existing same-direction edge → introduced cycle — mutating the graph only after all pass. The reported conflict is now the foremost *rule* hit anywhere in the batch (earliest submission position wins ties within a rule), regardless of where it sits. Atomicity is preserved.
- New `remove_dependencies()`: checks every listed direct edge exists first (first missing position → `DependencyError("dependency_not_found")`, graph untouched), then removes them all.

### `provenance_api/app.py`
- Split the batch handler into `_handle_dependencies_batch_post` (unchanged 201 behavior) and `_handle_dependencies_batch_delete`, sharing `_parse_dependency_batch_body()`.
- **DELETE** on `/resources/{id}/dependencies/batch`: same body rules (object with only `dependencies`, 1–100 non-empty separator-free distinct strings), 400 `invalid_request` for body/shape/query failures without reading data; start existence (404 `resource_not_found`) is checked before edge existence (404 `dependency_not_found`), never mixed; success returns 200 with per-edge echo in submission order, compact JSON ending in one newline. Other methods get 405 with `Allow: POST, DELETE`. All derived views (dependencies, impact, graph) recompute immediately; cursors unaffected.

### Tests & docs
- New `tests/test_dependency_batch_delete.py` (36 tests): success shape/order/compactness, atomicity, repeat-idempotence, 404 precedence, all 400 cases, 405 Allow, cursor/view preservation, plus registration-precedence tests proving cycle-at-position-0 loses to duplicate-edge rule and self-loop-last still wins.
- Updated the existing batch POST 405 test (`Allow: POST, DELETE`); rewrote the README batch sections with the new DELETE endpoint and fixed rule-order wording.

**Full suite: 1887 passed**, plus a live WSGI smoke test confirming the 200/404/400/405 responses and precedence end-to-end. Data remains in-memory only; no files written.
